thread:
pagerduty-bot: [PD] Trigger: GPU node flap / autoscaler thrash — oncall: @mike :rotating_light:

opsbot: Incident created: 1891004567, severity: P1 -> P2 (customer-impact: intermittent 5xx on hosted inference in us-west1). Paging oncall SRE.

mike: I'm on it, ack. seeing huge scale churn in us-west1-autoscale group.

lina: logs show a lot of pods OOMKilled with CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY in runtime logs. sample: 
```
[2026-03-02 15:02:11] runtime: kernel: %CUDA% CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY at infer_loop.cc:432
... stack ...
```

eva: autoscaler is bouncing from 6 -> 18 -> 4 nodes over last 6 minutes. metrics show massive short spike in in-flight tokens per instance causing scale triggers.

ryan: this matches recent traffic spike from a customer integration test. but why OOMs? should be constant per-request memory.

mike: hypothesis: rapid scale down removed warm nodes with cached KV, cold starts load model into mem causing transient OOM, then restart loops. also HPA has very short stabilizationWindow and aggressive target.

lina: digging into pod events: several ImagePullBackOffs? no, mostly CrashLoopBackOff with OOMKilled. one example: pod/serve-abc-5 crashed after failing to allocate 2.1G for attention cache.

opsbot: command run: kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep serve- | wc -l -> 12 alive, 7 restarting.

mike: immediate mitigation: increase min replicas to keep warm capacity. running `kubectl apply -f -` with patched deployment to set replicas: 8.

lina: applied replicas=8. also cordoning new preemptible nodes to avoid eviction thrash: `kubectl cordon ip-gpu-03` on nodes that are flapping.

eva: turning off autoscaler for this pool now (temporarily) to stop oscillation. `kubectl annotate hpa/autoscale-gpu alpha.autoscaler/disabled=true`

ryan: rolling restart of crashlooping pods in a controlled fashion to free GPU memory remnants: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/serve-runtime -n inference` — staggering 2 pods at a time.

mike: note: we observed keda/hpa using custom metric 'tokens_in_flight' with scaleUp/scaleDownThreshold too tight. recommend increasing stabilizationWindow and smoothing on custom metric.

lina: customer-impact confirmation: hosted inference latency spikes and 10% request 5xx rate for us-west customers between 15:00-15:10. reported by alerting.

opsbot: created ticket CS-5423 and added link to incident doc.

mike: watching logs now, CrashLoop frequency decreasing after min replicas and cordon. still seeing a couple of OOMs during pod initialization.

ryan: workaround: reduce per-model KV cache size config for this model to lower mem footprint until autoscaler behavior is tuned. patch config map: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  model.conf: |
    kv_cache_size: 512MB  # previously 1.5GB
```
```
kubectl apply -f model-cfg -n inference
```

lina: applied kv_cache_size=512MB for model v2. Logs now show less memory pressure, no new CUDA OOMs in the last 90s.

mike: changing autoscaler policy is next ops: increase minReplicas=6, maxReplicas=30 but add scaleDown stabilizationWindowSeconds=300 to avoid fast downscales. also add cooldown of 3m.

eva: running new HPA patch with `stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300` and `behavior: scaleDown: policies: - type: Percent value: 30 periodSeconds: 60`

opsbot: HPA patched. Observability: applied smoothing to custom metric aggregator (60s moving avg).

ryan: recommend longer-term changes: add prefix caching across pods so cold-start mem is lower, and add an LRU shared cache daemon on each node. filing follow-up with eng-runtime.

mike: temporary customer mitigation: route high-payload requests to dedicated pool (redwood-dedicated-1) which has fixed capacity and larger instance types. updating routing rule in gateway: `route:update --match region=us-west1 --backend=redwood-dedicated-1`

lina: gateway change applied. traffic rebalancing in progress, 60s to settle.

mike: oncall handoff in 20 minutes to @sre-rotation, will brief them: mitigation - min replicas raised, autoscale paused, kv reduced, code rollout restarted, customer routing to dedicated. we still need postmortem to tune autoscaler thresholds and add damping.

sre-rotation: ack, I'll take over. summary pls in msg. any outstanding customer tickets to escalate?

mike: CS-5423 open, CS asked for ETA on full restoration, told them 30-45m for steady state.

eva: monitoring: error rate down to 1.2% from 10%, latency trending to baseline. continue to monitor for 30m.

opsbot: Incident status changed to 'stabilized' at 1891004989 by mike.

sre-rotation: thanks, I'll keep eyes overnight and coordinate postmortem. suggest action items: 1) increase HPA stabilization config 2) add autoscaler damping/velocity checks 3) node allocation policy to prefer non-preemptible for critical pools 4) runtime change to lazy-kv-load.

mike: agreed. creating follow-up tickets: INF-2034 (autoscaler damping), INF-2035 (node allocation policy), INF-2036 (lazy-kv).

lina: marking incident as resolved for paging. will update incident doc and include replay logs and CLI commands used.

pagerduty-bot: Incident resolved by oncall at 1891005150.
